_meta.PRIMACY_RULE_APPLIED: Task §'What would prove this spoke wrong' requires code over prose. The code and the paper prose DISAGREE materially for BOTH datasets' recombination-to-element rule. Every 'condition' field below is transcribed from scripts/configs/datasplits.py at the pinned commit; the paper prose is recorded alongside as 'paper_prose_quote' with the discrepancy stated explicitly and NOT reconciled by bending either reading.

split_mechanics.description: Splits are pure deterministic boolean masks over the full factor grid. get_data_spliters(dataset, condition, variant) returns a (train_filter, test_filter) pair of callables f(latent_values, latent_classes) -> bool mask. Both datasets are exhaustive grids, so train and test are complements over the SAME image set; there is no held-out random sample and no third validation split.

factors.source: src/dataset/sprites.py at pinned commit, cross-checked against google-deepmind/dsprites-dataset README
factors.CRITICAL_COLUMN_NOTE: load_sprites DROPS the leading 'color' column at load time: latent_values = data_zip['latents_values'][:, 1:] and latent_classes = data_zip['latents_classes'][:, 1:]. Filters therefore receive 5-column arrays. The index constants in datasplits.py (shp,scl,rot,tx,ty = 0,1,2,3,4) are valid ONLY after this slice. Applying them to the raw 6-column npz arrays silently shifts every factor by one and yields a DIFFERENT (and for recomb2element, empty) split.

condition.name: recombination-to-element
condition.code_verbatim_test_filter:
((latent_classes[:, cls.shp] == 1) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.scl] > 0.6) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.rot] > 0.0) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.rot] < cls.a120) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.rot] > cls.a240) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.tx] > 0.66) &
 (latent_values[:, cls.ty] > 0.66))

ANGLE_CONSTANT_TRAP.status: PINNED (verified by two independent fetches of the same line via different CDNs)
ANGLE_CONSTANT_TRAP.explanation: The angle constant NAMES are bound to SWAPPED values in the source. a120 = 4*pi/3 = 4.18879 rad = 240 degrees; a240 = 2*pi/3 = 2.09440 rad = 120 degrees. Read naively, the clause '(rot < a120) & (rot > a240)' looks logically impossible; with the actual bound values it means 120deg < rotation < 240deg, which MATCHES the paper's section 2.1 prose. Do not 'fix' the names.
ANGLE_CONSTANT_TRAP.effective_rotation_rule: 2*np.pi/3 < orientation < 4*np.pi/3, i.e. 120 deg < theta < 240 deg, strict on both ends

condition.train_filter: logical NOT of the test filter (train = complement of test over the full 737280-image grid)

terms.note: redundant term, subsumed by the interval above

condition.paper_prose_quote: "In the dSprites dataset, for testing the Recombination-to-element case, we split each range of values of a generative factor into three bins, so that we had 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 243 such combinations of bins for all five generative factors. We then remove one of these 243 combinations during training, namely those that satisfied [shape=ellipsis, position-x >= 0.6, , position-y >= 0.6, 120 <= rotation <= 240 , scale < 0.6]."
condition.paper_prose_locator: Section 2.1 'Image reconstruction with dSprites dataset', p.4

paper_prose_secondary_quotes.quote: "In dSprites, an example of this case would be excluding the combination: [shape=ellipse, scale=1, orientation< 120, position-x>0.5, position-y>0.5] from the training set - i.e. the model has never seen a large ellipse at < 120 in the bottom-right corner, though it has seen all other combinations."
"Left) Recombination-to-Element condition where the models did not see [shape = ellipse, scale = 1, orientation < 120 , position-x > 0.5, position-y > 0.5]"

PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.verdict: DIRECT CONTRADICTION in sign. Code and the p.3 narrative gloss ('a LARGE ellipse') and Fig.2 caption ('scale = 1') all point to the LARGE end; the sec 2.1 'scale < 0.6' is almost certainly a typo in the paper. Code is authoritative. NOT reconciled by adjusting the code reading.

PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.prose_p3_and_fig2: orientation < 120 deg (CONTRADICTS both the code and sec 2.1)
PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.verdict: The paper contradicts ITSELF on rotation: sec 2.1 says 120-240, p.3 and Fig.2 say <120. Code agrees with sec 2.1. Code is authoritative.
Three different thresholds across the paper; code uses 0.66. Code is authoritative.

PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.code: thresholds are NOT exact tertiles: scale > 0.6 selects 4 of 6 values (two thirds), not one third
PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.prose: 'three bins ... 243 combinations ... remove one of these 243'
PROSE_VS_CODE_DISCREPANCIES.verdict: The implemented cell is NOT 1/243 of the grid. 737280/243 = 3034.9 expected under the prose; the code's cell contains 5808 images (~1.9x). The '243 bins' framing is a post-hoc description that the shipped code does not implement exactly.

FLOAT_BOUNDARY_HAZARD.severity: HIGH — affects n_test by up to +17%
FLOAT_BOUNDARY_HAZARD.scale_term: 'scale > 0.6' sits EXACTLY on a stored grid value. Whether the stored float64 for 0.6 compares strictly greater than the literal 0.6 decides 4 vs 5 scale values, i.e. n_test 5808 vs 7260. My count assumes stored 0.6 is NOT > 0.6 (the mathematically intended reading).
FLOAT_BOUNDARY_HAZARD.orientation_terms: The 120deg/240deg bounds land EXACTLY on grid indices 13 and 26 of np.linspace(0,2*pi,40) in exact arithmetic. Strict inequalities exclude them, giving 12 values; float64 round-off in linspace vs 2*np.pi/3 could admit one or both, giving 13 or 14 values (n_test 6292 or 6776).

randomised.note: No seed, no sampling, no shuffling enters the split. The filters are deterministic boolean masks. The Sacred 'seed' config governs model init / data-loader shuffling only, not split membership.

recombination_to_range.SHAPE_ARRAY_TRAP: This condition indexes latent_VALUES for shape (values 1.0/2.0/3.0), so '== 1' means SQUARE. The recomb2element condition indexes latent_CLASSES (values 0/1/2), so '== 1' there means ELLIPSE. Same literal, different shape. This is not a bug — it correctly reproduces the paper, which uses square for recomb-to-range and ellipse for recomb-to-element. Getting this wrong silently swaps the held-out shape.
recombination_to_range.paper_prose_quote: "First, we excluded all combinations where [shape=square, position-x>0.5]. The model sees other shapes at those positions during training and it sees squares on the left-hand side of the screen."
recombination_to_range.other_variants_in_paper_not_reported: "In the second case, we excluded all combinations where [shape=square, scale>0.5]. In the third case, we excluded all combinations where [shape=square, rotation > 90 ]. We observed very similar results for all three cases and below we report the results for the first variant." (Section 2.1, p.4). Only shape2tx was found in the pinned datasplits.py under recomb2range for Dsprites; the scale and rotation variants were NOT located in code — status NOT OBTAINED for those two.

extrapolation.paper_prose_quote: "Finally, for the Extrapolation case, we excluded all combinations of generative factors where [position-x > x]. We chose a set of different values for x: x in 0.16, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, where x is normalised in the range [0, 1] (results shown in Figure 2 for x = 0.50)."
extrapolation.note: Only the x = 0.5 variant is present in the pinned code; the 0.16/0.25/0.75 variants are NOT OBTAINED from code.
